findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed half and half to be missing the date marking. 
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).
Date mark was added to the half and half.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Both soda gun nozzles are observed soiled with accumulation. Soda gun nozzle was cleaned and sanitizer at the time of the inspection to correct the violation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Food contact surface is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: Observed an open container of half and half that was not marked with the date it was opened. Date mark all ready to eat, time and temperature control for safety foods with the date of opening and hold no longer than 7 days maximum.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: Observed wood shelving behind the bar that is in need of repair as these shelves are no longer smooth, nonabsorbent and easily cleanable. Clean and seal these wood shelves.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19  (C) Nonfood-contact surfaces are no longer easily cleanable. Replace with an corrosion-resistant, nonabsorbent and smooth material meeting National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI certification for use within a foodservice facility.  Reference 4-101.19.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: Observed the soda guns to be soiled with food debris. Clean at a frequency to maintain free of accumulated soil. 750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use and any time they may have become contaminated.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed the soda gun holders to have some soil accumulated in the bottoms. Clean and maintain free of accumulation. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed boxes of single use cups on the floor in the basement. Store these items. 750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.
Observed unwrapped straws on the bar top. 750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user. Provide either dispenser or wrapped straws to protect these single service items

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Thermometer could not be located in the beer cooler used for storage of half and half and whipped topping. Thermometer from downstairs fridge was placed in the beer cooler.
Provide functioning thermometers for both the fridge and the beer cooler used for storage of potentially hazardous foods.

All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Soda guns had chunky mold buildup. Soda guns were manually cleaned and sanitized during the inspection (quat solution used for in-place sanitizing = 200ppm). Nozzles and holders were placed through ware washing cycle in dish machine (50ppm chlorine).
Clean and sanitize the soda gun, nozzles, and holders as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

Food and equipment must be protected from cross contamination at all times.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
750.290 - Ice scoops were stored with food contact surface in direct contact with outside surfaces of Red Bull cans (cans were in a holder in the ice bin - scoops were lodged between cans and inner edge of holder). Ice scoops were placed through ware washing cycle in the dish machine.
Store scoops with handles extended up out of the ice or on a clean dry surface. The outer surface of any bottled or canned beverages is not considered a clean surface.


Ice scoops shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - Facility does not have quat test strips for use with quat tablets. Bartender noted the quat tablets are only used for soaking mats and not actually used for sanitizing dishes (all items ran through dish machine). Quat test strips must be obtained for use with quat tablets (i.e. sanitizing soda guns, etc.). Bleach may be used instead of quat tablets - bleach solutions would require use of the same test strips needed to check the chlorine based sanitizer at the dish machine.

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of each chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solutions in parts per million.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - Thermometer was not present in beer cooler used for storage of half and half and whipped topping. Provide a thermometer for the cooler. All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3F.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Bottles of beer were observed inside ice bin. The ice is used for customer drinks. Bottles were removed from the ice bins. Cans of Red Bull were observed in a corner container in one ice bin, and the bartender noted the plastic container is ran through the dish machine between uses. Food, including ice, shall be protected from contamination at all times. Do not store bottles or cans inside the ice used for customer drinks. The outside surfaces of bottles and cans are not considered clean/sanitary surfaces.

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.comment: 750.830a - Detergent bucket was observed to be empty. Bartender switched out empty bucket with one from the basement that was approximately a quarter full. Bartender was advised on monitoring and maintaining chemicals at the dish machine. Dish machines shall be properly installed and maintained in good repair. Utensils and equipment placed in the dish machine shall be exposed to all dishwashing cycles. **Prime the chemical lines when buckets of sanitizer and detergent are changed out to ensure product is properly dispensing. If possible, change out buckets prior to detergent and sanitizer running dry to maintain a constant supply of chemicals within the lines and avoid potential air bubbles/dispensing issues.**

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: 750.830g - Chlorine test kit was not available for checking dish machine sanitizer concentration. Machine was not properly sanitizing but was corrected during the inspection (see #20a). Bottle of test strips were shown to bartender and concentrations for dish machine (50ppm) versus clean/sanitize in place items such as the soda gun (100ppm) were discussed. Obtain and use chlorine test strips. A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.830 - Dish machine sanitizing concentration was at 0ppm chlorine. Full bucket of sanitizer was hooked up to the chemical dispensing line. After priming the line the sanitizer concentration was at 50ppm. General dish machine maintenance, including monitoring chemical buckets, priming lines when buckets are changed out, and checking sanitizer concentration daily, were discussed. Chemical sanitizers in dish machines must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized. 
Obtain and use test strips to monitor the sanitizing concentration in the dish machine.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled: A) soda guns, nozzles and holders (mold) & B) inside ice machine around ceiling at the drip guard and attachment screws (mold). Properly clean and sanitize the aforementioned food contact surfaces as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of mold.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text: 750.840 - Glass removed from dishwasher was being dried with a common towel. Bartender drying the glass was new/unaware air drying of glasses is required. Manager noted the water spots of dry glasses are typically polished away using a clean cloth intended for such. Polishing after ware washing (including last step of air drying) is completed is ok. Make sure all glasses are properly cleaned and sanitized and allowed to air dry prior to polishing away water spots. All equipment and tableware shall be air dried.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text: 750.1120 & 1110d - Paper towels were not available at the handsink. Bartender noted hands are typically dried using common cloth towel. Bartender was advised on proper handwashing technique and informed the use of common towels is a critical violation and is prohibited. A roll of paper towels was placed at the handsink. Maintain supplies of soap and paper towels at the handsinks to allow for proper handwashing, and do not use common towels for drying/wiping hands. B) Toilets in women's room were soiled around top of water line in the bowel and around the top of inner porcelain. Clean toilets daily/as needed. Toilet facilities shall be kept clean and in good repair and free of objectionable odors.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the cutting board at the bar to have many nicks ,cuts, and grooves. Replace  the cutting board.
750-650a Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.
